table.name: Breeds
table.purpose: Lookup table of dog breeds, referenced by the Dogs table. Each row is one breed with a short code and its full name.

breed_code.name: breed_code
breed_code.description: Primary key. Short three-letter code identifying a dog breed (e.g. ESK = Eskimo, HUS = Husky, BUL = Bulldog). Referenced by Dogs.breed_code.

breed_name.name: breed_name
breed_name.description: Full display name of the breed corresponding to the breed code.

table.name: Charges
table.purpose: Lookup/price list of veterinary charges: each row is a billable charge type with a fixed amount (likely in whole currency units, e.g. cents or dollars). Used to price treatments for dogs in a veterinary clinic database (related tables: Dogs, Owners, Treatments, Treatment_Types, Professionals).

charge_amount.name: charge_amount
charge_amount.description: Price of the charge in whole currency units (e.g. dollars or cents; unit not determinable from data). Values: 98, 322, 640.

charge_id.name: charge_id
charge_id.description: Primary key of the charge; surrogate integer identifier.

charge_type.name: charge_type
charge_type.description: Name of the charge category, e.g. 'Daily Accommodation', 'Drugs', 'Health Check'.

table.name: Dogs
table.purpose: Animal-shelter / kennel register: one row per dog, tracking its arrival at the facility, adoption by an owner, and departure, with breed, size, and physical attributes. Referenced by Treatments for medical care records.

abandoned_yn.name: abandoned_flag
abandoned_yn.description: Flag indicating whether the dog was abandoned (1) or not (0); 3 of 15 dogs are flagged as abandoned.

age.name: age_years
age.description: Age of the dog in whole years (values 1-9).

breed_code.name: breed_code
breed_code.description: Foreign key to Breeds.breed_code; three-letter code for the dog's breed (ESK=Eskimo, HUS=Husky, BUL=Bulldog).

date_adopted.name: adoption_date
date_adopted.description: Timestamp when the dog was adopted; all values fall in Feb-Mar 2018, after arrival and before/at departure.

date_arrived.name: arrival_date
date_arrived.description: Timestamp when the dog arrived at the shelter/kennel (Apr 2017 - Jan 2018).

date_departed.name: departure_date
date_departed.description: Timestamp when the dog left the facility; all departures cluster on 2018-03-24/25, suggesting a batch export or closing event rather than individual departures.

dog_id.name: dog_id
dog_id.description: Primary key identifying each dog; referenced by Treatments.dog_id.

gender.name: gender
gender.description: Binary gender flag (0/1); which value maps to male vs female is not determinable from the data.

name.name: name
name.description: Dog's given name; all unique in this sample.

owner_id.name: owner_id
owner_id.description: Foreign key to Owners.owner_id, the adopting owner; some owners have multiple dogs (e.g. owner 14 with 3).

size_code.name: size_code
size_code.description: Foreign key to Sizes.size_code; dog's size category (SML=Small, MED=Medium, LGE=Large).

weight.name: weight
weight.description: Dog's weight, numeric 1.39-9.8; unit not stated (likely kg, though values are low for large dogs, so possibly a synthetic or scaled value).

table.name: Owners
table.purpose: Pet owners registered at a veterinary clinic; each row is one dog owner with contact and address details, referenced by the Dogs table.

cell_number.name: cell_number
cell_number.description: Owner's mobile phone number, stored as text in varied formats (with extensions, country codes, punctuation).

home_phone.name: home_phone
home_phone.description: Owner's home/landline phone number, stored as text in varied formats.

owner_id.name: owner_id
owner_id.description: Primary key identifying the owner; referenced by Dogs.owner_id (one owner may have many dogs).

state.name: state
state.description: Owner's U.S. state of residence (names written without spaces, e.g. 'NorthDakota', 'NewYork').

street.name: street
street.description: Owner's street address including house number, street name, and unit/apartment/suite.

zip_code.name: zip_code
zip_code.description: Owner's U.S. ZIP code (5-digit, stored as text with leading zeros).

table.name: Professionals
table.purpose: Staff members of a veterinary clinic (veterinarians and other employees) who perform treatments on dogs; each row is one professional, referenced by the Treatments table.

cell_number.name: cell_number
cell_number.description: Mobile phone number of the professional, stored as text in varied formats (with extensions, parentheses, dashes).

home_phone.name: home_phone
home_phone.description: Home/landline phone number of the professional, stored as text in varied formats.

professional_id.name: professional_id
professional_id.description: Primary key identifying the professional; referenced by Treatments.professional_id (the professional who performed each treatment).

role_code.name: role_code
role_code.description: Job role of the professional: 'Veterenarian' (sic, misspelled Veterinarian) or 'Employee' (non-veterinarian staff).

state.name: state
state.description: US state of the professional's address (full state names, sometimes without spaces, e.g. 'NorthCarolina').

street.name: street
street.description: Street portion of the professional's mailing address; values often embed city/state/ZIP on following lines, so the column is not strictly street-only.

zip_code.name: zip_code
zip_code.description: US ZIP code of the professional's address (5-digit, stored as text with leading zeros).

table.name: Sizes
table.purpose: Lookup table of dog size categories, referenced by Dogs.size_code. Each row is one size category with a code and its full description.

size_code.name: size_code
size_code.description: Primary key. Abbreviated size category code: SML = Small, MED = Medium, LGE = Large. Referenced by Dogs.size_code.

size_description.name: size_description
size_description.description: Full label of the size category corresponding to the code (Small, Medium, Large).

table.name: Treatment_Types
table.purpose: Lookup table of treatment/service types offered to dogs (e.g., exams, vaccinations, walks), referenced by the Treatments table in a veterinary/dog-care database.

treatment_type_code.name: treatment_type_code
treatment_type_code.description: Short code identifying the treatment type (EXAM, VAC, WALK); primary key, referenced by Treatments.treatment_type_code.

treatment_type_description.name: treatment_type_description
treatment_type_description.description: Human-readable description of the treatment type (e.g., 'Physical examination', 'Vaccination', 'Take for a Walk').

table.name: Treatments
table.purpose: Records individual treatment/medical service events performed on dogs by professionals, with the type of treatment, date, and cost. Each row is one treatment event for one dog by one professional.

cost_of_treatment.name: cost_of_treatment
cost_of_treatment.description: Cost charged for the treatment event, in whole currency units (e.g., dollars). Values range 139–945 with a median of 429; no decimals observed, so the exact currency is unknown.

date_of_treatment.name: date_of_treatment
date_of_treatment.description: Timestamp (date and time) when the treatment was performed. Stored as VARCHAR but values are valid timestamps; range 2018-02-26 to 2018-03-24.

dog_id.name: dog_id
dog_id.description: Foreign key to Dogs.dog_id identifying the dog that received the treatment (many treatments per dog).

professional_id.name: professional_id
professional_id.description: Foreign key to Professionals.professional_id identifying the staff member who performed the treatment.

treatment_id.name: treatment_id
treatment_id.description: Primary key; unique identifier for each treatment event (1–15).

treatment_type_code.name: treatment_type_code
treatment_type_code.description: Foreign key to Treatment_Types.treatment_type_code. Codes: EXAM = Physical examination, VAC = Vaccination, WALK = Take for a Walk.
